Summary: Invite-based user onboarding (Platform / Tenant)
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Replace the temp-password POST /users flow with an invite-based onboarding path covering platform (superadmin) and tenant (admin) levels, widen roles to supervisor/agent, and add case-insensitive email uniqueness. Source: .sdlc/user-onboarding-hierarchy/03-tasks.md

Summary: Widen users_role_check to include supervisor/agent and add users.team
Description / Acceptance Criteria: psql -f database/schema.sql run twice in a row against a seeded dev DB both succeed with no error, and INSERT INTO users (..., role) VALUES (..., 'supervisor') succeeds while role='bogus' still fails the CHECK.

Summary: Drop the case-sensitive users_email_key constraint
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Applying the file leaves \d users showing no users_email_key, and inserting two live rows differing only in case succeeds (proving the old constraint is gone) before the next step re-guards it.

Summary: Add guarded lower-casing email backfill with collision detection
Description / Acceptance Criteria: A test seeding Bob@x.com and bob@x.com as live rows makes schema.sql raise the named exception and leaves the table unmodified (lesson 5), and a fixture with only one of them applies cleanly with the row lower-cased.

Summary: Add partial unique index users_email_lower_idx on lower(email) WHERE deleted_at IS NULL
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Two soft-deleted rows sharing a lower-cased address are allowed, a second live row at that address is rejected, and re-running schema.sql is a no-op (CREATE UNIQUE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS).

Summary: Create user_invites table plus its two indexes
Description / Acceptance Criteria: schema.sql applied twice is a no-op both times; two pending invites for the same email in the same tenant collide with UniqueViolationError; two pending invites for the same email in DIFFERENT tenants both insert successfully (lesson 3 — scope check). Indexes: user_invites_pending_email_idx scoped per-tenant via COALESCE(tenant_id, '00000...'), and user_invites_tenant_idx.

Summary: Split get_current_user into get_authenticated_user and a console-gated get_current_user
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Introduce CONSOLE_ROLES = frozenset({'superadmin','admin','viewer'}); switch routers/auth.py's /auth/me and /auth/change-password to Depends(get_authenticated_user). Done when: a supervisor and an agent JWT get 403 from GET /users, /provider-configs, /carriers, /calls, /audit-log, but 200/204 from /auth/me and /auth/change-password; a viewer JWT (including is_service_account=true, tenant_id=None) still gets 200 on those reads; unauthenticated GET /health, /auth/setup-status, POST /auth/login, POST /auth/bootstrap all still reach their handlers with no 401/403 from the gate; and a test enumerates every route in the app and asserts exactly two depend on get_authenticated_user. Scope this tripwire test to route enumeration driven off the shared deps module rather than a Config-app-only assumption, since Knowledge/DID/Campaigns import this same module (lesson 9).

Summary: Add may_invite() privilege-escalation guard
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Signature: may_invite(*, actor_role, actor_tenant_id, target_role, target_tenant_id) -> bool. Done when the privilege-escalation matrix test passes: tenant_admin->superadmin denied (AC2); tenant_admin->any role with tenant_id != actor's, including tenant_id=None, denied (AC3); tenant_admin->{tenant_admin,supervisor,agent,viewer} in own tenant allowed (AC4); superadmin->tenant_admin anywhere and ->superadmin allowed; supervisor/agent as actor denied for every target; and every role in users_role_check is explicitly classified as console or non-console by a companion assertion.

Summary: Add _new_token() invite token generator (urlsafe + sha256)
Description / Acceptance Criteria: _new_token() = secrets.token_urlsafe(32) -> (raw, sha256_hex). Done when: a test asserts the raw token is >=43 chars, 1000 calls produce zero hash collisions, and the raw value never appears in any log record, response body or audit_log row produced elsewhere in the suite.

Summary: Add create_invite, resend_invite, revoke_invite with tenant-blind conflict handling
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Each calls may_invite with the STORED row's role/tenant for resend/revoke, 404 first if the row is absent; plus the tenant-scoped conflict check (409 flat string for tenant_admin, tenant-naming 409 for super_admin) and the UniqueViolationError->409 mapping for a concurrent double-send. Done when: a tenant_admin inviting an email that exists in another tenant gets exactly {"detail": "this email cannot be invited"} with no tenant slug/name/id in the body, byte-identical to the response for an email with a pending invite in the actor's own tenant; the same request as super_admin names the tenant; and a tenant_admin resend/revoke of a Tenant B invite id, or of a superadmin invite, returns 403 (IDOR test, AC2/AC3 replayed against stored rows). create_invite returns the row and raw token only — email delivery is invoked by the router in Phase 3, not here.

Summary: Add accept_invite() atomic three-step transaction
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Implements: classify row -> conditional UPDATE ... WHERE status='pending' AND expires_at > now() RETURNING * -> _insert_user -> set accepted_user_id -> write_audit; catching the users-table UniqueViolationError as EmailTaken WITHOUT burning the invite. Done when: two simultaneous accept_invite calls with the same token produce exactly one accepted row and one InviteUsed raised (asserted as distinct from expired/revoked), with exactly one row in users; a squatting scenario (Tenant A and Tenant B both holding a pending invite for the same email) has the second accept raise EmailTaken with a tenant-blind message and leave that invite still pending (resendable/revocable) rather than 500ing; and expired/revoked/already-accepted tokens each raise their own named exception, distinctly.

Summary: Add team column to _insert_user()
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Done when existing test_users.py cases pass unchanged (POST /users is untouched here — its removal is a Phase 3 task, once the invite path is reachable). NOTE: the email lower-casing in _insert_user and get_user_by_email originally scoped here MOVED INTO Phase 1 (T4's review fix) because users_email_lower_idx cannot ship without it — do not re-do it here.

Summary: Add token_hash to the audit redaction set
Description / Acceptance Criteria: An accept/resend/revoke test inspects the written audit_log row and asserts token_hash is absent/redacted while entity_type/action/actor are present.

Summary: Add InviteCreate / InviteAccept schemas and widen UserUpdate role Literal
Description / Acceptance Criteria: InviteAccept carries password: str = Field(min_length=8). Done when: InviteAccept(password="short") raises a validation error and password="12345678" does not; UserUpdate(role="supervisor") validates.

Summary: Widen Role Literal to include supervisor and agent
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Widen Role = Literal["superadmin","admin","viewer"] to include "supervisor","agent". Done when: mypy/type-check on services/config passes and a JWT payload carrying role="supervisor" type-checks as Role (no runtime behavior change; this closes the stale-Literal drift the design flagged as deprioritized).

Summary: Add send_invite_email() via stdlib smtplib with secret-ref SMTP password
Phase: Phase 3: API, email delivery and cutover
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Reads SMTP_HOST/PORT/USER/FROM and SMTP_PASSWORD_REF via the repo's existing secret-ref resolver (libs/config_sdk/secrets.py), and documents the new env vars alongside INVITE_BASE_URL. Done when: with SMTP mocked to raise, calling send_invite_email() directly raises/returns a failure the caller can catch without crashing; with SMTP mocked to succeed, the composed message body contains ${INVITE_BASE_URL}/invite#<token> with the token ONLY in the fragment, never in a path segment.

Summary: Add authenticated invite management routes (POST/GET /invites, resend, revoke)
Phase: Phase 3: API, email delivery and cutover
Description / Acceptance Criteria: POST /invites, GET /invites (super_admin sees all; tenant-scoped actor's ?tenant_id= ignored/forced to JWT), POST /invites/{id}/resend, POST /invites/{id}/revoke, all under require_role("superadmin","admin"); the create/resend handlers call send_invite_email() after commit, non-fatal on failure. Done when: GET /invites?tenant_id=<other> as a tenant_admin returns only the actor's own tenant's invites (AC11); the same call as super_admin, unfiltered, returns invites across tenants; POST /invites returns 201 with email_sent: bool in the body; and with SMTP mocked to raise, POST /invites still returns 201 email_sent: false with the row status='pending' and resendable (AC12).

Summary: Add public GET/POST /invites/accept with X-Invite-Token header
Phase: Phase 3: API, email delivery and cutover
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Token via X-Invite-Token header, no JWT dependency; returns only {email, tenant_name, role, status} on GET. Done when: a request with no Authorization header reaches both handlers (proving they bypass the console gate by construction); GET /invites/accept for a valid token returns no field naming any other account or tenant beyond the invitee's own; and accepting with a wrong/missing header/token structure 404s.

Summary: Add per-inviter fixed-window throttle for invite create/resend
Phase: Phase 3: API, email delivery and cutover
Description / Acceptance Criteria: In-process fixed-window throttle helper keyed on invited_by: 30 attempts/hour outcome-blind probe cap; 20 successful sends/hour across create+resend; 60s per-invite resend cooldown off last_sent_at. Done when: 30 consecutive create attempts that each 409 make the 31st 429 with Retry-After; a successful create attempt after 30 conflicts is ALSO 429 (proving outcome-blindness); 20 successful sends make the 21st 429 even with probe-counter room left; and two resends within 60s make the second 429 naming remaining seconds.

Summary: Add accept-route IP throttle, mount invites router, delete POST /users
Phase: Phase 3: API, email delivery and cutover
Description / Acceptance Criteria: IP throttle keyed on request.client.host (NEVER X-Forwarded-For), 10/minute and 50/hour across GET+POST, plus the one-line comment documenting the trusted-proxy caveat; wire app.include_router(invites.router); and, now that the new path is reachable, delete POST /users (temp-password path). Done when: the 11th accept request from one IP in a minute is 429, byte-identical for a valid and an invalid token; a forged X-Forwarded-For header does not move the request into a different bucket than an identical request without it; POST /invites and POST /invites/accept are reachable end-to-end through the app; POST /users returns 404/405; and existing test_users.py cases for the deleted route are removed with the remaining suite passing — leaving a tenant able to onboard a user via invite at every point after this task, with no gap where neither path works.

Summary: Add Invite/User types and invite API client functions
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Add Invite/User types and listUsers, listInvites, createInvite, resendInvite, revokeInvite, getInvite, acceptInvite. Done when: each function has a corresponding unit/integration test (or existing request()-pattern test) hitting a mocked endpoint and returning the typed shape, matching how other lib/api.ts functions are covered today.

Summary: Build users + pending-invites management screen
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Invite modal, resend disabled during cooldown, status column pending/expired/revoked/accepted. Done when: the nav item renders only for superadmin/admin roles; the page lists users and invites scoped to the viewer's tenant (or all tenants for super_admin, AC11); and an invite shown as email_sent: false still displays as pending with a working resend action (AC12).

Summary: Build public invite accept page reading token from location.hash
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Sends the token as X-Invite-Token on GET/POST /invites/accept; treat /invite as a standalone unguarded route like /login. Done when: visiting /invite#<token> while unauthenticated does not bounce to /login; submitting a valid password calls POST /invites/accept with the token in the header and NEVER in the URL/query string; and an expired/revoked/already-used token renders its specific message (AC6, AC10).

Summary: Add remaining invite integration coverage (soft-delete re-invite, normalization, audit rows)
Description / Acceptance Criteria: Coverage not already produced as 'done when' checks above: soft-delete re-invite (invite -> accept -> soft-delete -> re-invite -> second live row, old row's password no longer authenticates); normalization (Bob@X.com invite resolves/blocks against bob@x.com account); and the audit-row-per-mutating-path assertion across create/resend/revoke/accept. Done when: all listed scenarios pass in pytest services/config/tests/.
